newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony seen reporting robust Q1 earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Sony seen reporting robust Q1 earnings growth.

text.p: Sony Corp's business is continuing to sail along on a good wind, with the electronics giant likely to report a 30 percent to 60 percent rise in operating profits for the first business quarter, analysts say.
Many of them expect Sony to revise upward its forecast for the year to March 31, 1998, later this year.

Sony, which in May surprised the market with a 160 percent jump in group net profits for the last business year, will release earnings results for the April-June quarter of the 1997/98 business year on July 31.

"Sony's business is steadily expanding, benefiting from continuing strong demand for its digital audio-visual products, particularly in the domestic market," said Hitoshi Kuriyama, an analyst at Goldman Sachs (Japan) Corp.
"Despite some uncertainties in the second half regarding the yen rate and the economy, there is still much room for upward revisions."
Analysts expect Sony's group operating profit in the April-June quarter to reach 74 billion yen to 88 billion yen, up from 55.32 billion yen a year earlier.
Their forecasts for Sony's group net profit ranged from 23 billion yen to 34.5 billion yen, up from the year-earlier result of 17.1 billion yen.
Sony, which relies on overseas markets for 70 percent of its sales, has benefited from the yen's weakening over the past two years, they said.

A substantial foreign exchange profit is likely in the first quarter as well, as Sony had made currency hedging arrangements around 121 yen for 60 percent of its trade for the quarter, analysts said. The yen in recent weeks has traded at a rate of 110 to 118 to the dollar.
Buoyed by speculation about robust earnings, Sony's share price climbed to a record high of 11,200 yen in early Monday morning trade.

"I'm positive about Sony's earnings for the first and second quarters," said Masaru Koshida, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "I see no factors in the short term that could pour cold water on the strong upward momentum in its share price."

Koshida expects Sony's group operating profit in the electronics sector to grow by 50 percent to around 62 billion yen in the first quarter, while profit from the entertainment sector will remain flat at about 17 billion yen.

Sony, considered particularly strong in digital audio-visual technology, last year benefited greatly from strong domestic demand for new generations of digital AV products such as video cameras and mini disks.
According to a Nihon Keizai Shimbun survey, Sony had a 50 percent market share in both digital video cameras and mini disks in the domestic market in fiscal 1996/97.
Strong sales of such products boosted Sony's operating profits in the domestic market by 76 percent in 1996/97, Sony said.
Sony plans to introduce its new digital AV products in overseas markets during the current business year.
